gameName: Sid Meier's Civilization: The Board Game

provenance.author: BoardFlow
sources: Sid Meier's Civilization rulebook (FFG, via RulesPal)

steps.text: Learning game: box Egypt, Rome and all wonders; the game ends when someone builds their third city
Deal civilization sheets at random (or pick, if all agree); each player picks a colour
Each: 6 armies, 2 scouts, 3 city markers, 4 military tech markers, 36 tech cards, a reference sheet, a setup card and 4 government cards
Market board at one end: shuffle the 4 unit decks onto it; give each player 1 artillery, 1 infantry, 1 mounted facedown as standing forces
Each player's artillery, infantry and mounted markers one-stripe side up below those decks; aircraft marker star side down
Building markers sorted onto their spaces
Wonder deck: modern facedown, medieval on top; 4 ancient wonders faceup below it, each with its marker
steps.note: Egypt first takes a random ancient wonder; a medieval one fills the gap

steps.text: Culture event decks (ancient, medieval, modern) shuffled below the culture track; each leader marker on its start space
{n} of each market resource token by the board; box the rest
Home tiles faceup in front of their owners as the diagram shows; deal the neutral tiles facedown to complete the map
Great people, huts and villages: three facedown mixed piles
Culture, wound and coin tokens in piles; combat bonus cards, Space Flight and disaster markers faceup nearby
Capital on one of the 4 centre squares of your home tile (first game: the starting arrow), unwalled side up
1 army and 1 scout in your capital's outskirts (not on water)
Starting tech from your civilization sheet faceup as the base of your tech pyramid
Government cards stacked with Despotism faceup on top
Trade dial: the trade symbols in your capital's 8 outskirts squares
Economy dial on 0 (or the coins you already have)
1 city marker, 5 armies and 1 scout beside your sheet; the last city waits for Irrigation
America
details: Great person: a random one, placed in your capital's outskirts at the end of setup

steps.text: China
details: Walls: capital starts walled side up

steps.text: Egypt
details: Wonder: a random ancient wonder, its marker in your capital's outskirts

steps.text: Germany
details: Troops: 2 extra infantry units in your standing forces

steps.text: Rome
details: Republic: start with Republic instead of Despotism

steps.text: Russia
details: Extra army: the white army figure, placed with your others
Communism: start with Communism instead of Despotism

steps.text: You collect trade again on the first turn
Each new tech level must sit on two techs of the level below
The first player marker does not pass on turn 1
First player: whoever traces their family back the furthest (or random)
